formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: An integral domain R is a Dedekind domain in this factorization characterization if every nonzero ideal factors as a finite product of nonzero prime ideals and this decomposition is unique up to permuting the factors.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: A nonzero nonunit element p of an integral domain R is a prime element when the principal ideal (p) is a prime ideal; equivalently, p divides ab only if p divides a or p divides b.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

meanings.context: Commutative algebra: unique factorization domain

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: An integral domain R is a unique factorization domain when every nonzero nonunit factors into finitely many irreducibles, and any two such factorizations agree after reordering factors and multiplying them by units.

meanings.context: cardinality

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

meanings.context: Commutative algebra: clopen subsets of an affine spectrum

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: For a commutative ring R, a subset U of Spec(R) is simultaneously open and closed exactly when there is an idempotent e of R (so e²=e) such that U=D(e)={p in Spec(R):e is not in p}; this e is unique.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: In a category C, an object X is categorically compact if for every filtered diagram M_i whose colimit exists, the natural map colim_i Hom_C(X,M_i) → Hom_C(X,colim_i M_i) is bijective.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

formulations.text: For a ring map R→S and prime q of S, the map is G-unramified at q if there exists g outside q such that R→S_g is G-unramified.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

meanings.context: Commutative algebra: unramified at a target prime

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: For a ring map R→S and a prime ideal q in S, the map is unramified at q if some g in S outside q makes the localized map R→S_g unramified.

meanings.grouping_note: Distinct semantic label retained; later cross-page synonym/variant refinement remains open.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

meanings.grouping_note: Distinct semantic label retained; later cross-page synonym/variant refinement remains open.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: For a monoid G and a field L, an L-valued multiplicative character of G is a homomorphism from G to the multiplicative monoid of L; in particular it sends the identity of G to 1 and respects multiplication.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: A family (x_i) of elements of a field extension K/k is algebraically independent over k when the evaluation homomorphism k[X_i:i∈I]→K, sending each indeterminate X_i to x_i, is injective.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: Given K/k, the base field k is algebraically closed in K when every element of K algebraic over k already belongs to k; equivalently, its relative algebraic closure in K equals k.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: An extension K/k is purely transcendental if it is isomorphic as an extension of k to the field of rational functions in an arbitrary set of algebraically independent indeterminates over k.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: For a field extension K/k, the algebraic closure of k inside K is the intermediate subfield consisting of all elements of K that are algebraic over k; this is a relative, not necessarily algebraically closed, field.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.
formulations.text: A transcendence basis B of K over k is an algebraically independent subset B⊆K for which every element of K is algebraic over the subfield k(B) generated by k and B.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

formulations.text: Given a ring homomorphism R→S and an S-module M, its flat locus relative to R is the subset of Spec(S) consisting of primes q for which the localization M_q is flat as an R-module, equivalently as an R_p-module for p=q∩R.

formulations.editorial_note: Independently paraphrased from the cited source and reviewed as a source-backed mathematical candidate; not human-refereed.

The Hilbert polynomial is eventually computed from composition lengths of graded quotient modules.
The Hilbert–Samuel function is defined by module lengths of successive quotients.
An ideal of definition uses the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring.
Equidimensionality requires irreducible components to have the same Krull dimension.
Topological Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets.
Local Krull dimension is defined by minimizing the Krull dimension of open neighbourhoods.
The universal scheme fibre-product construction is a categorical pullback specialized to schemes.
Scheme morphisms are morphisms of locally ringed spaces with suitable stalk homomorphisms.
A categorical fibre product is a limit of a diagram shaped as a cospan.
The nowhere-dense criterion tests emptiness of the interior of a subset's closure.
The affine tensor-product construction identifies the fibre product of affine schemes over an affine base.
The coordinate ring of an affine fibre product is the tensor product of its algebra factors.
The injectivity locus is defined for maps between finite projective modules.
The injectivity locus is a subset of the prime spectrum of the base ring.
Surjectivity of the module map is tested after localization at a prime ideal.
The surjectivity locus is indexed by prime ideals of the ring spectrum.
The relative global complete-intersection condition requires a presentation by finitely many generators and relations.
Syntomicity explicitly requires flatness of the underlying ring homomorphism.
Syntomicity also explicitly requires a finitely presented ring homomorphism.
The fibres of a syntomic map are required to be local complete-intersection algebras over their residue fields.
The constructible subset is defined in the prime spectrum of a commutative ring.
The finite-field definition refers to the cardinality of the underlying finite set.
The Mittag-Leffler directed-system condition is expressed through Mittag-Leffler inverse systems of Hom modules.
The directed system is specifically required to consist of finitely presented modules.
The definition uses injectivity of the tensor-product comparison map for arbitrary families of modules.
Cofinality measures the least order type or cardinal size of a cofinal subset.
The equivalent definition of cofinality uses the smallest cardinality of a cofinal subset.
The quotient of a direct sum is an explicit realization of the categorical colimit in modules.
The family of module transition maps is a direct or inductive system indexed by a preorder.
The coequalizer is a special colimit of a parallel-pair diagram.
Algebraicity of an element is defined relative to an extension field and its base field.
An algebraic extension is characterized by each of its elements being algebraic over the base field.
Every finite-presentation ring map has finitely many algebra generators and is consequently of finite type.
The Cohen–Macaulay local-ring criterion compares module depth with ring dimension.
The Cohen–Macaulay equality requires the Krull dimension of the local ring.
The ring is Cohen–Macaulay when all prime-localized rings satisfy the local Cohen–Macaulay property.
The global Cohen–Macaulay condition is explicitly restricted to Noetherian commutative rings.
The constructible or patch topology is defined on an underlying spectral space.
The patch topology is generated using a subbasis consisting of quasi-compact opens and their complements.
A spectral map has both domain and codomain spectral spaces.
Its defining continuity condition preserves quasi-compactness of open subsets under inverse image.
Spectral spaces are required to be quasi-compact as topological spaces.
Quasi-compact open subsets must form a basis for the spectral-space topology.
The local sections in the gluing condition belong to localized modules on standard open sets.
Gluing data compare localizations of modules on pairwise standard-open overlaps.
A connected limit or colimit is defined by connectedness of its indexing category.
This formulation states the same finite-generation property of an R-module using a finite generating list.
This formulation gives the same finite-module-presentation condition using a short finite-free presentation.
The prime subfield is classified by the characteristic of the ambient field.
The Serre R_k condition requires sufficiently low-height prime localizations to be regular local rings.
The index bound in Serre R_k is imposed on the heights of prime ideals.
The module Serre S_k condition compares local depths at all primes against dimension.
The module S_k condition measures the Krull dimension of the localized module support.
The ring S_k condition is imposed through lower bounds on local depth.
This Serre condition is stated for Noetherian coefficient rings.
Serre's normality criterion explicitly requires condition R_1 at codimension-one points.
Serre's normality criterion explicitly requires condition S_2 on ring depths.
Serre's criterion gives an equivalent characterization of normal Noetherian rings.
The valuative uniqueness condition tests maps out of arbitrary valuation rings.
Separatedness is defined by closedness of the diagonal into the fibre product.
The comma categories in the cofinality criterion must be nonempty and connected.
The comma categories in the initial-functor criterion must be nonempty and connected.
A generic point is attached to an irreducible closed subset and is dense there.
An irreducible component is maximal among the irreducible subsets.
A dimension function is constrained by the specialization order on points.
The unit decrement property is required on immediate specializations.
Immediate specialization is defined by the absence of points strictly between two related points.
Formal smoothness of a field extension is the ring-map lifting property specialized to field extensions.
The localization of a category is constructed by inverting arrows from a multiplicative system.
The common-root test for coprimeness is conducted over an algebraic closure of the coefficient field.
Flatness is defined by exactness preservation under tensoring with the module.
The Cohen–Macaulay module property compares local depth with dimension of module support.
The dimension in this Cohen–Macaulay test is the Krull dimension of the module support.
The global property requires every prime localization to satisfy the local module Cohen–Macaulay condition.
Maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules are characterized by depth equal to dimension of the ambient local ring.
The maximal Cohen–Macaulay condition compares depth with ring Krull dimension rather than support dimension.
The correspondence relates morphisms of affine schemes to ring homomorphisms in the opposite direction.
The morphisms in the affine correspondence are between prime spectra of rings.
The classification describes irreducible components of a topological space, specialized to ring spectra.
The irreducible-component classification is for the prime spectrum of the ring.
Local constructibility requires constructibility on each member of an open cover.
A split fibred groupoid must first be a category fibred in groupoids.
Symbolic prime powers are defined by taking ordinary powers in the localized ring and contracting back.
A coefficient ring is a complete local subring of the ambient complete local ring.
The Cohen ring definition requires a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p.
The complete-local-ring property is defined for a local ring and its maximal ideal.
Completeness is equivalently identified by comparing the ring with its maximal-ideal-adic completion.
The going-down condition uses inclusion chains of primes of the source spectrum.
The going-up condition uses inclusion chains of primes of the source spectrum.
A category-valued presheaf is defined by a contravariant functor into categories.
A split fibred category must first be a Grothendieck fibration over its base.
A splitting arises from a strict contravariant category-valued functor through Grothendieck construction.
A discrete valuation ring is a valuation ring with the specified discrete ordered value group.
Domination is defined for an inclusion of local rings by contraction of maximal ideals.
Perfectness is defined by requiring that all algebraic extensions be separable.
Limit ordinals are a special kind of ordinal characterized by not being successors.
The limit-ordinal criterion excludes the successor of any smaller ordinal.
A successor ordinal is constructed by adjoining the previous ordinal as an element.
The graded module construction presupposes a nonnegatively graded coefficient ring.
This summand condition is an equivalent characterization of projectivity, not a separate kind of projective module.
The dimension of a finite module is defined as the Krull dimension of its support.
The dimension of a module uses topological Krull dimension of the support subspace.
The finite-module support is the module support notion specialized to a finitely generated module.
The special support statement is explicitly restricted to finitely generated modules.
Local freeness is defined by asking module localizations to be free on a cover.
A contravariant functor from C is an ordinary functor defined on the opposite category.
The representable presheaf is a functor whose source is the opposite category.
A representable presheaf is a contravariant functor given by Hom into an object.
The Zariski topology on a scheme is specified by requiring affine charts to carry the prime-spectrum topology.
The Zariski topology is defined on the underlying space of a scheme.
Categories over a fixed base form a strict 2-category with projection-preserving functors and natural transformations.
Universal closedness of a continuous map is tested after arbitrary pullbacks, which are categorical fibre products.
The quasi-regular sequence criterion compares naturally graded modules over a polynomial coefficient ring.
The Hom-functor criterion for projectivity depends on exactness of the represented functor in the category of modules.
The Bourbaki-properness criterion is expressed through products of topological spaces and the induced product map.
The diagonal criterion uses the product topological space X×X, a categorical product in the category of spaces.

observations.context_hint: algebraic closure
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Given a field F, an algebraic closure of F is an extension field K containing F in which every element is algebraic over F and every nonconstant polynomial over K has a root in K.

observations.context_hint: algebraically closed
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A field K is algebraically closed precisely when it has no proper algebraic field extension; equivalently, each nonconstant one-variable polynomial with coefficients in K admits a root in K.

observations.context_hint: topology basis
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a topological space X, a basis is a family B of open sets such that, whenever an open U contains x, some member of B contains x and is itself contained in U.

observations.context_hint: topology subbasis
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A subbasis for an existing topology on X is a family of open subsets whose finite intersections form a basis for that topology, with the empty intersection taken as X.

observations.context_hint: affine scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An affine scheme is a locally ringed space isomorphic to the prime spectrum of a commutative ring equipped with its structure sheaf.

observations.context_hint: initial object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: In a category C, an object I is initial if every object Y of C is the target of exactly one morphism originating at I.

observations.context_hint: final object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: In a category C, an object T is terminal (final) if for every object Y of C there is exactly one morphism from Y to T.

observations.context_hint: cardinality
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a set A, its cardinality may be represented by the smallest ordinal equipotent to A, meaning the least ordinal for which a bijection with A exists.

observations.context_hint: minimal polynomial
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: If an element alpha of an extension E/k is algebraic over k, its minimal polynomial over k is the unique monic polynomial generating the kernel of evaluation k[t] to E at alpha; it is irreducible over k.

observations.context_hint: splitting field
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a nonconstant polynomial P over a field F, a splitting field is a field extension E/F in which P factors into linear terms and which is generated over F by all its roots.

observations.context_hint: noetherian topological space
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological space is Noetherian when every descending sequence of its closed subsets eventually becomes constant.

observations.context_hint: quasicompact space
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological space X is quasi-compact if each open cover of X contains a finite subcollection that still covers X; no Hausdorff condition is required.

observations.context_hint: quasicompact map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A continuous map f:X to Y is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of Y is quasi-compact in X.

observations.context_hint: spectrum ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a commutative ring R, the prime spectrum Spec(R) is the set consisting of all prime ideals of R, equipped with the Zariski topology whose closed sets comprise the common zero-locus sets V(I).

observations.context_hint: exact functor
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A functor between categories with the requisite finite limits and colimits is exact if it preserves both finite limits and finite colimits (equivalently it is both left exact and right exact).

observations.context_hint: finite field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A field extension E/F has degree equal to the vector-space dimension of E over F; the extension is finite exactly when this dimension is a finite integer.

observations.context_hint: left adjoint
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For functors L:C to D and R:D to C, L is left adjoint to R when there are bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C, natural in both X and Y.

observations.context_hint: tensor algebra
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For an R-module M, its tensor algebra is the graded associative R-algebra obtained by taking the direct sum over n at least zero of the n-fold tensor powers of M, with the degree-zero summand R and multiplication by concatenation of tensors.

observations.context_hint: normal integral domain
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An integral domain R is normal when every element of its fraction field that satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in R already belongs to R.

observations.context_hint: normal ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A commutative ring R is normal if each localization R_p at a prime ideal p is an integrally closed domain in its own fraction field.

observations.context_hint: associated prime
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is associated to M if p is the annihilator ideal of some element of M.

observations.context_hint: purely inseparable extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a field F of characteristic p greater than zero, an extension K/F is purely inseparable if, for every alpha in K, some p-power alpha^(p^n) lies in F. The trivial extension is also purely inseparable in any characteristic.

observations.context_hint: locally closed immersion
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A morphism of schemes is a locally closed immersion if it admits a factorization through a closed immersion followed by an open immersion.

observations.context_hint: artin schreier extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a field K of prime characteristic p, an Artin-Schreier extension is obtained by adjoining a solution of t^p - t = a, for a in K; a nontrivial such extension has cyclic Galois group of order p.

observations.context_hint: locally ringed space
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A locally ringed space is a topological space X together with a sheaf of rings O_X whose stalk at every point of X is a local ring.

observations.context_hint: locally ringed space morphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A morphism of locally ringed spaces consists of a continuous map and a compatible morphism of structure sheaves, with induced maps on all stalks required to be local ring homomorphisms.

observations.context_hint: coherent ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring R is coherent if every finitely generated ideal of R admits a finite presentation as an R-module.

observations.context_hint: primitive element
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a finite field extension E/F, a primitive element is an element alpha of E such that the smallest subfield containing F and alpha is all of E.

observations.context_hint: linearly disjoint extensions
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: If fields K and L extend k inside a common field, K and L are linearly disjoint over k when the multiplication map from their tensor product over k to their compositum KL is injective.

observations.context_hint: pushout
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Given morphisms B to A and B to C in a category, a pushout is an object P equipped with morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B, such that every other compatible pair of maps to an object T factors uniquely through P.

observations.context_hint: monomorphism of schemes
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A morphism f:X to Y of schemes is a monomorphism when for every scheme T and two morphisms g,h:T to X, equality f composed with g = f composed with h forces g=h.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: locally nilpotent (nil) ideal
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An ideal I in a commutative ring R is locally nilpotent (in the Stacks Project terminology) when each element x of I is nilpotent, with the exponent allowed to depend on x.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: nilpotent ideal
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An ideal I of a ring R is nilpotent when there is a single positive integer n for which the product ideal I^n is the zero ideal.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Jacobson ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A commutative ring R is a Jacobson ring when every radical ideal I of R equals the intersection of the maximal ideals of R containing I.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: equivalent prime-ideal test
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Equivalently, a commutative ring R is Jacobson if each prime ideal p is the intersection of all maximal ideals containing p.

observations.context_hint: Infinite Galois theory: Krull topology on an absolute or relative Galois group
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a Galois extension E/F, the Krull topology on Gal(E/F) is the weakest topology making every evaluation map sigma ↦ sigma(a), for a in E, continuous when E is discrete. With this topology the Galois group is profinite.

observations.context_hint: Topology: constructible subset of a Noetherian space
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: If X is a Noetherian topological space, a subset C of X is constructible exactly when C can be expressed as a finite union of sets U∩F, where U is open in X and F is closed in X.

observations.context_hint: Factorization in integral domains: associate elements
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Two elements a and b of an integral domain R are associates if a=ub for some invertible element u of R.

observations.context_hint: Factorization in integral domains: irreducible element
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An element r of an integral domain R is irreducible if it is nonzero and not a unit and every factorization r=ab has at least one unit factor.

observations.context_hint: Factorization in integral domains: prime element
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A nonzero nonunit element p of an integral domain R is a prime element when the principal ideal (p) is a prime ideal; equivalently, p divides ab only if p divides a or p divides b.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: unique factorization domain
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An integral domain R is a unique factorization domain when every nonzero nonunit factors into finitely many irreducibles, and any two such factorizations agree after reordering factors and multiplying them by units.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: principal ideal domain
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An integral domain R is a principal ideal domain if every ideal of R can be generated by a single element.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: ideal-factorization characterization of Dedekind domain
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An integral domain R is a Dedekind domain in this factorization characterization if every nonzero ideal factors as a finite product of nonzero prime ideals and this decomposition is unique up to permuting the factors.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: clopen subsets of an affine spectrum
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a commutative ring R, a subset U of Spec(R) is simultaneously open and closed exactly when there is an idempotent e of R (so e²=e) such that U=D(e)={p in Spec(R):e is not in p}; this e is unique.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: categorically compact or finitely presentable object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: In a category C, an object X is categorically compact if for every filtered diagram M_i whose colimit exists, the natural map colim_i Hom_C(X,M_i) → Hom_C(X,colim_i M_i) is bijective.

observations.context_hint: Higher category theory: strict (2,1)-category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A strict (2,1)-category is a strict 2-category in which each 2-morphism is invertible with respect to vertical composition, so every hom-category is a groupoid.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: unramified ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A homomorphism of commutative rings R→S is unramified in the Stacks Project convention when S is finitely generated as an R-algebra and the module of Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R} is zero.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: G-unramified ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is G-unramified in the Stacks Project convention if it is of finite presentation and Ω_{S/R}=0.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: unramified at a target prime
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a ring map R→S and a prime ideal q in S, the map is unramified at q if some g in S outside q makes the localized map R→S_g unramified.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: G-unramified at a target prime
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a ring map R→S and prime q of S, the map is G-unramified at q if there exists g outside q such that R→S_g is G-unramified.

observations.context_hint: Algebra: field-valued multiplicative character of a monoid
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a monoid G and a field L, an L-valued multiplicative character of G is a homomorphism from G to the multiplicative monoid of L; in particular it sends the identity of G to 1 and respects multiplication.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: algebraic independence over a base field
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A family (x_i) of elements of a field extension K/k is algebraically independent over k when the evaluation homomorphism k[X_i:i∈I]→K, sending each indeterminate X_i to x_i, is injective.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: purely transcendental extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An extension K/k is purely transcendental if it is isomorphic as an extension of k to the field of rational functions in an arbitrary set of algebraically independent indeterminates over k.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: transcendence basis
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A transcendence basis B of K over k is an algebraically independent subset B⊆K for which every element of K is algebraic over the subfield k(B) generated by k and B.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: transcendence degree
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: The transcendence degree trdeg_k(K) of a field extension K/k is the cardinality of any transcendence basis of K over k, independent of the particular basis chosen.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: relative algebraic closure inside an extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a field extension K/k, the algebraic closure of k inside K is the intermediate subfield consisting of all elements of K that are algebraic over k; this is a relative, not necessarily algebraically closed, field.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: relatively algebraically closed subfield
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Given K/k, the base field k is algebraically closed in K when every element of K algebraic over k already belongs to k; equivalently, its relative algebraic closure in K equals k.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: flat locus of an S-module over a base ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Given a ring homomorphism R→S and an S-module M, its flat locus relative to R is the subset of Spec(S) consisting of primes q for which the localization M_q is flat as an R-module, equivalently as an R_p-module for p=q∩R.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: covariant set-valued representable functor
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A covariant functor F:C→Sets is representable if there exists an object X of C together with a natural isomorphism F(Y)≅Hom_C(X,Y) for every object Y in C.

observations.context_hint: Set theory and algebraic geometry: cardinal size of a scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: The size of a scheme S in the Stacks Project's set-theoretic convention is max(aleph_0,κ_1,κ_2), where κ_1 counts affine open subsets of S and κ_2 is the supremum of cardinalities of their rings of global sections.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: naive cotangent complex of a ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a ring map R→S, let P=R[X_s:s∈S] map canonically onto S and put I=ker(P→S). The naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} is the two-term complex I/I²→Ω_{P/R}⊗_P S, with I/I² in homological degree 1 and the induced differential from universal derivation.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: universal homeomorphism induced by a ring map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A homomorphism of commutative rings R→S induces a universal homeomorphism on spectra if for every R-algebra R′ the canonical map Spec(S⊗_R R′)→Spec(R′) is a homeomorphism.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: regular Noetherian local ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Definition 10.60.10 (00KU), referenced at start of Section 10.106
observations.text: A Noetherian local ring (R,m) of Krull dimension d is regular local if m can be generated by d elements; equivalently dim_{R/m}(m/m²)=d.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: regular system of parameters
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: In a regular Noetherian local ring (R,m) of dimension d, a regular system of parameters is a d-element sequence in m that generates the maximal ideal m.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: flat module, filtered-colimit characterization
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is flat if and only if M is a filtered colimit of finite-rank free R-modules; this is Lazard's equivalent characterization of the usual exactness-preservation definition of flatness.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: weakly associated prime ideal of a module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is weakly associated to M if some element m∈M has p among the prime ideals minimal over its annihilator Ann_R(m).

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: On X=Spec(R), a quasi-coherent O_X-module is an O_X-module isomorphic to the sheaf ~M associated with some R-module M; for every standard open D(f), the sections of ~M on D(f) identify with the localization M_f.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, its I-adic completion R^ is the inverse limit of the quotient rings R/I^n over positive integers n, with transition maps given by reduction modulo smaller powers.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For an R-module M and ideal I⊆R, the I-adic completion of M is lim_n M/I^n M; its elements can be viewed as mutually compatible residue classes modulo powers of I.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adically complete module or ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is I-adically complete when its canonical map M→lim_n M/I^n M is an isomorphism; a ring R is I-adically complete when it has this property as its own module.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Tor-based local criterion for module flatness
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a local map of Noetherian local rings R→S with residue field k of R and a finitely generated S-module M, M is flat over R if and only if Tor_1^R(k,M)=0.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: finite prime field of characteristic p
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a prime integer p, the finite prime field F_p is the quotient field Z/(p), whose elements are integer residue classes modulo p with operations inherited from integers.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: quotient field construction from an irreducible polynomial
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a field k and irreducible polynomial f in k[x], the quotient k[x]/(f) is a field extending k, obtained by adjoining the class of x as a root of f.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: chain and length of prime ideals
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A chain of prime ideals of R is a strictly increasing finite sequence p_0⊊p_1⊊⋯⊊p_n; its length is the number n of strict inclusions.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Krull dimension of a ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: The Krull dimension of a commutative ring R is the supremum of the lengths of all finite strict chains of prime ideals in R, with the value infinite when those lengths are unbounded.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: height of a prime ideal
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R, the height of p is the Krull dimension of the local ring R_p, equivalently the supremum of lengths of strict prime chains terminating at p.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: system of parameters of a Noetherian local ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A system of parameters of a Noetherian local ring (R,m) of dimension d is a sequence of d elements of m whose generated ideal is m-primary, also called an ideal of definition.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: functor of points of a scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a scheme X, its functor of points is the contravariant functor h_X from schemes to sets that assigns to a scheme T the set Hom_Sch(T,X), with pullback along T'→T defined by precomposition.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: T-valued point of a scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A T-valued point of a scheme X is a scheme morphism T→X; for T=Spec(k) with k a field, such a point is a map from the spectrum of k into X.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: Galois field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A field extension E/F is Galois if it is algebraic, separable, and normal over F; for finite extensions this is equivalent to having precisely [E:F] F-automorphisms.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: Galois group of an extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a Galois extension E/F, the Galois group Gal(E/F) is the group of all field automorphisms of E that fix each element of F, with group law given by composition.

observations.context_hint: Graded commutative algebra: homogeneous ideal
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a graded ring S=⊕_d S_d, an ideal I is homogeneous if it is graded as an S-submodule; equivalently, every homogeneous component of every element of I also belongs to I.

observations.context_hint: Graded commutative algebra: homogeneous spectrum Proj(S)
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a nonnegatively graded commutative ring S, Proj(S) is the topological space of homogeneous prime ideals that do not contain the irrelevant ideal S_+=⊕_{n>0}S_n, equipped with the subspace topology inherited from Spec(S).

observations.context_hint: Graded commutative algebra: degree-zero homogeneous localization
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a positively graded ring S and homogeneous element f of positive degree, S_(f) denotes the degree-zero subring of the graded localization S_f, consisting of fractions a/f^n with deg(a)=n·deg(f).

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: standard étale ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring map R→S is standard étale when S is isomorphic as an R-algebra to R[x]_g/(f) for a monic polynomial f∈R[x] and polynomial g∈R[x], with f′ invertible in R[x]_g/(f).

observations.context_hint: Category theory: covering family in a Grothendieck site
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a site (C,Cov), a covering family of an object U is a collection of arrows {U_i→U} included in Cov(U), where the designated covering families contain isomorphism covers and are stable under compositional refinement and pullback along arrows into U.

observations.context_hint: Grothendieck sites: combinatorially equivalent covering families
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Section 3.11 paragraph before Lemma 3.11.1; Sites Definition 7.8.2
observations.text: Two families (f_i:U_i→U) and (g_j:V_j→U) are combinatorially equivalent when every map in either family occurs in the other, ignoring multiplicities and the indexing sets; equivalently each family admits an indexing map into the other identifying the arrows.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: geometrically normal algebra
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically normal over a field k if for every extension of fields K/k the base-changed algebra K⊗_k A is a normal ring.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: alternative perfect-closure test for geometric normality
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Equivalently, a k-algebra A is geometrically normal if its scalar extension k^perf⊗_k A to the perfect closure of k is a normal ring; this also tests normality over all finite purely inseparable field extensions.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: direct-sum transfinite dévissage
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A direct sum dévissage of an R-module M is an ordinal-indexed increasing family of submodules M_α starting at zero, continuous at limit ordinals and with union M, such that each successor inclusion M_α⊆M_{α+1} splits as a direct summand.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: Kaplansky transfinite dévissage
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A Kaplansky dévissage of an R-module M is a direct sum dévissage whose every successive quotient M_{α+1}/M_α is a countably generated R-module.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: geometrically irreducible k-algebra
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically irreducible over the field k when, for every field extension K/k, the ring A⊗_k K has exactly one minimal prime ideal, equivalently its prime spectrum is irreducible.

observations.context_hint: Homological algebra: derived tensor/Tor module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For modules M and N over a commutative ring R and integer i≥0, Tor_i^R(M,N) is the ith homology module of F_•⊗_R N, where F_• is any free resolution of M; its isomorphism type is independent of that resolution.

observations.context_hint: Homological algebra: Tor-vanishing criterion for module flatness
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is flat if and only if Tor_1^R(M,R/I)=0 for every finitely generated ideal I⊆R; equivalently, Tor_i^R(M,N)=0 for all R-modules N and every i>0.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: monoidal category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Definition 4.43.3; unit and associativity constraints in Section 4.43
observations.text: A monoidal category consists of a category C, a bifunctor ⊗:C×C→C, a natural associativity isomorphism satisfying the pentagon, and a unit object 1 with natural unit isomorphisms satisfying the triangle coherence identity.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: strong monoidal functor
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A strong monoidal functor F:C→D between monoidal categories is a functor equipped with coherent natural isomorphisms F(X)⊗F(Y)≅F(X⊗Y) and a compatible identification of F(1_C) with the unit in D.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: tensor-invertible monoidal object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An object X in a monoidal category is tensor-invertible if there exists an object Y with X⊗Y≅1 and Y⊗X≅1, where 1 is the unit object.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: left dual of a monoidal object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A left dual Y of an object X in a monoidal category comes with maps η:1→X⊗Y and ε:Y⊗X→1 for which the resulting two triangle, or snake, composites on X and Y are the respective identity maps.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: symmetric monoidal category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A symmetric monoidal category is a monoidal category equipped with a natural exchange isomorphism X⊗Y→Y⊗X that is involutive and compatible with the associator through the required coherence diagrams.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: symmetry-preserving strong monoidal functor
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A symmetric monoidal functor is a strong monoidal functor between symmetric monoidal categories whose structural tensor isomorphisms also commute with the symmetry/exchange isomorphisms of the two categories.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: essentially constant filtered diagram/ind-object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A filtered diagram M_i with cocone M_i→X is essentially constant with value X if some stage M_i admits a map X→M_i splitting M_i→X, and for every stage j the maps from M_j into a later common stage eventually agree with those factoring through X and the chosen M_i.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: essentially constant inverse diagram/pro-object
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A cofiltered diagram M_i with cone X→M_i is essentially constant with value X if some stage M_i maps back to X splitting X→M_i, and for each stage j there exists a common earlier stage where the transition maps factor through X and the selected M_i.

observations.context_hint: Linear algebra: characteristic polynomial of a square matrix
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: The characteristic polynomial of an n×n matrix A over a commutative ring R is the polynomial χ_A(t)=det(t I_n−A) in R[t], where I_n denotes the identity matrix.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: smooth homomorphism of rings
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A homomorphism R→S of commutative rings is smooth when S is finitely presented as an R-algebra and the naive cotangent complex of S over R is quasi-isomorphic to a finite projective S-module concentrated in degree zero.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: binary coproduct of objects
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A coproduct of objects X,Y in a category C is an object P together with maps i:X→P and j:Y→P such that for any Z and arrows f:X→Z and g:Y→Z there is a unique h:P→Z satisfying h∘i=f and h∘j=g.

observations.context_hint: Topology: codimension of an irreducible closed subset
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For an irreducible closed subset Y of a topological space X, codim(Y,X) is the supremum of lengths of strict chains Y=Y_0⊊Y_1⊊⋯⊊Y_n of irreducible closed subsets of X; it may be infinite.

observations.context_hint: Topology: catenary space
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological space X is catenary if between each pair of nested irreducible closed subsets Y⊆Z, the codimension codim(Y,Z) is finite and all maximal chains of irreducible closed subsets connecting Y to Z have the same length.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: discrete category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A category C is discrete if every morphism in C is an identity morphism; consequently it has no arrows between distinct objects and no nonidentity endomorphisms.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: category fibred in sets
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A category p:E→C is fibred in sets over C when p is a category fibred in groupoids and each fibre E_U over an object U of C is a discrete category.

observations.context_hint: Higher category theory: 2-category of categories fibred in sets
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a base category C, the 2-category of categories fibred in sets over C has such fibrations as objects, functors commuting with their projections to C as 1-morphisms, and natural transformations lying over identity arrows as 2-morphisms.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: quasi-finite ring map at a prime
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Let R→S be a finite-type ring homomorphism and q∈Spec(S) lying over p∈Spec(R). The map is quasi-finite at q if q is an isolated point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)); equivalently its local fibre has dimension zero.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: internal Hom module of two R-modules
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For modules M,N over a commutative ring R, the internal Hom Hom_R(M,N) is the R-module of R-linear homomorphisms M→N, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication (r·f)(m)=r·f(m).

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: open immersion of locally ringed spaces
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A morphism f:(X,O_X)→(Y,O_Y) of locally ringed spaces is an open immersion if f is a homeomorphism of X onto an open subset of Y and the induced morphism f^{-1}O_Y→O_X is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: open locally ringed subspace
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For an open subset U of the underlying space of a locally ringed space (X,O_X), its open subspace is the locally ringed space (U,O_X|_U) obtained by restricting the structure sheaf to U.

observations.context_hint: Homological algebra: snake lemma connecting homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a commutative diagram of abelian groups with exact rows X→Y→Z→0 and 0→U→V→W and vertical maps α,β,γ, the snake connecting map ∂:ker(γ)→coker(α) sends z to the class of an element u∈U whose image in V equals β(y), where y∈Y maps to z; this class is independent of the choices.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: base change of a ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For ring homomorphisms R→S and R→R′, the base change of R→S along R→R′ is the induced homomorphism R′→S⊗_R R′.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: base change of a module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Given an R-algebra S, an S-module M and a map R→R′, the base change of M along R→R′ is the module M⊗_R R′ over S⊗_R R′.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: universally Japanese ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring R is universally Japanese if every finite-type R-algebra S that is an integral domain is Japanese (N-2), meaning the integral closure of S in any finite extension of its fraction field is finite over S.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Nagata ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A commutative ring R is Nagata if it is Noetherian and R/p is Japanese (N-2) for each prime ideal p of R.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: relative dimension of a finite-type ring map at a prime
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a finite-type ring map R→S and prime q of S lying over p in R, the relative dimension at q is the local topological dimension at the corresponding point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)).

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: relative dimension of a ring map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: The relative dimension of a finite-type ring homomorphism R→S is the supremum over all primes q∈Spec(S) of its relative fibre dimensions dim_q(S/R).

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: pure ideal
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An ideal I in a commutative ring R is pure if the quotient module R/I is flat over R.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: equivalent ideal-intersection criterion for purity
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Equivalently, an ideal I⊆R is pure when I∩J=IJ for every ideal J of R; it is enough to test finitely generated ideals J.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: algebra of finite presentation
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-algebra S is finitely presented if it admits a presentation S≅R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) with finitely many generators x_i and finitely many polynomial relations f_j.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: finitely presented module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is finitely presented if an exact sequence R^m→R^n→M→0 exists with both m and n finite; equivalently M has finitely many generators and relations.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: rank of a finite-free-module map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a homomorphism φ:R^m→R^n of finite free modules, its rank is the largest integer r for which the induced exterior-power map ∧^rφ is nonzero (and is zero when φ itself is zero).

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: ideal of maximal nonzero-size minors
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a homomorphism φ:R^m→R^n of rank r, its maximal-rank determinantal ideal I(φ) is the ideal of R generated by all r×r minors of a matrix representing φ; by convention it equals R when r=0.

observations.context_hint: Higher category theory: final object of a (2,1)-category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A final object T of a (2,1)-category C is an object such that, for every Y in C, there is a 1-morphism Y→T and any two such 1-morphisms are connected by exactly one 2-morphism.

observations.context_hint: Higher category theory: 2-fibre product in a (2,1)-category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For 1-morphisms X→Z←Y in a (2,1)-category, a 2-fibre product X×_Z Y is a terminal object, in the 2-categorical sense, among objects W equipped with maps W→X and W→Y and an invertible 2-morphism between the two resulting maps W→Z.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: iso-comma construction of a 2-fibre product
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For functors F:A→C and G:B→C, their iso-comma category A×_C B has triples (a,b,α:F(a)≅G(b)) as objects and compatible pairs of arrows in A and B as morphisms.

observations.context_hint: Topology: Stone–Čech compactification by universal property
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Section 5.25 introductory universal property and subsequent product construction
observations.text: A Stone–Čech compactification of a topological space X (in this source's universal-map sense) is a continuous map η:X→βX into a compact Hausdorff space βX such that every continuous f:X→K with K compact Hausdorff factors uniquely through a continuous map βX→K.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: trace of an element in a finite field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a finite extension L/K and α∈L, the field trace Tr_{L/K}(α) is the trace over K of the K-linear endomorphism of L given by multiplication x↦αx.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: norm of an element in a finite field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a finite extension L/K and α∈L, the field norm N_{L/K}(α) is the determinant over K of the multiplication-by-α endomorphism L→L.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: formally unramified ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is formally unramified if, for every R-algebra A and square-zero ideal I⊆A, any R-algebra map S→A/I admits at most one lift to an R-algebra map S→A.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: differential characterization of formal unramifiedness
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is formally unramified exactly when its module of Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R} is zero.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: smooth ring homomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A homomorphism R→S of commutative rings is smooth if S is finitely presented as an R-algebra and the naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} is quasi-isomorphic to a finite projective S-module in degree zero.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: local ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A nonzero commutative ring R is local if it possesses exactly one maximal ideal.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: nonunit characterization of a local ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Equivalently, a nonzero commutative ring R is local if the set of its nonunits is an ideal; this ideal is necessarily the ring's unique maximal ideal.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: zerodivisor and regular element
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Section 10.25 introductory discussion of zero divisors
observations.text: An element r of a commutative ring R is a zerodivisor when some nonzero element s∈R satisfies rs=0; a nonzerodivisor is an element for which multiplication by r on R is injective.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: total quotient ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Section 10.25 introductory total ring of fractions construction
observations.text: The total quotient ring Q(R) of a commutative ring R is the localization S^{-1}R at the multiplicative set S of all nonzerodivisors of R, allowing fractions with any regular denominator.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: finite limit
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A limit of a diagram F:I→C is a finite limit if the indexing category I has finitely many objects and finitely many morphisms, including identities.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

observations.text: For a set-valued diagram F:I→Sets, its limit is the subset of the Cartesian product ∏_i F(i) consisting of families (x_i) satisfying F(u)(x_i)=x_j for every arrow u:i→j in I.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: colimit of a diagram of sets
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Section 4.15 explicit formula for colimit in Sets
observations.text: For a set-valued diagram F:I→Sets, its colimit is the disjoint union of the sets F(i), modulo the equivalence relation generated by x∼F(u)(x) for each arrow u:i→j.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: algebraic field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An extension K/k of fields is algebraic if every element α∈K satisfies a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in k.

observations.text: An algebraic extension K/k is separable if the minimal polynomial of each α∈K has no repeated roots over an algebraic closure of k.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An algebraic field extension K/k in characteristic p>0 is purely inseparable if every α∈K has α^(p^n)∈k for some integer n≥0.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: normal algebraic extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An algebraic extension K/k is normal if every irreducible polynomial over k having one root in K splits completely into linear factors over K.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: Galois field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An algebraic extension K/k is Galois precisely when it is both separable and normal over k.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: representable category fibred in groupoids
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A category p:S→C fibred in groupoids is representable if there exists an object X of C and an equivalence over C between S and the slice category C/X.

observations.text: For a category C, its 2-category of categories over C has as objects functors p:S→C, as 1-morphisms functors G:S→S′ satisfying p′G=p, and as 2-morphisms natural transformations between such functors whose components project to identity morphisms in C.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: functor representable by a scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A contravariant functor F:Sch^op→Sets is representable by a scheme if some scheme X admits a natural isomorphism F(T)≅Hom_Sch(T,X) for every scheme T.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: separably generated extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A field extension K/k is separably generated if there exists a transcendence basis B⊆K over k such that K is a separable algebraic extension of the rational-function field k(B).

observations.context_hint: Field theory: separable extension not necessarily algebraic

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Cohen–Macaulay locus of the spectrum
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

observations.text: For a formally unramified ring map R→S, a universal square-zero thickening is a surjective R-algebra map S′→S with square-zero kernel such that every R-algebra map S→A/I, for any square-zero ideal I of A, has a unique compatible lift S′→A.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: category fibred in groupoids
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A functor p:E→C is a category fibred in groupoids if every morphism f:V→U in C lifts to a morphism y→x above f for each object x over U, and each compatible base morphism between the sources of two arrows into x lifts uniquely to a morphism between their domains.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: universally closed scheme morphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S is universally closed if for every morphism S′→S the induced base-change map X×_S S′→S′ sends closed subsets to closed subsets.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: filtered colimit of étale ring maps
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-algebra A is a filtered colimit of étale R-algebras if there exists a filtered diagram of étale R-algebras (A_i) and an R-algebra isomorphism A≅colim_i A_i.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: closed unions of connected components of Spec(R)
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A subset T of Spec(R) is closed and a union of connected components if and only if it can be expressed as V(I) for an ideal I generated by idempotent elements of R.

observations.context_hint: Topology: topological group
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological group is a group G with a topology under which the multiplication map G×G→G and inversion map G→G are both continuous.

observations.context_hint: Topology: profinite group
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A profinite group is a topological group that is isomorphic as a topological group to an inverse limit of finite discrete topological groups.

observations.context_hint: Topology: topological ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological ring is a ring R with a topology for which its addition R×R→R and multiplication R×R→R are continuous maps.

observations.context_hint: Topology: module over a topological ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Given a topological ring R, a topological R-module is an R-module M endowed with a topology such that addition M×M→M and scalar multiplication R×M→M are continuous.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: descent/gluing data for schemes

observations.text: Gluing data for schemes comprises schemes X_i, open subschemes U_ij⊆X_i, and isomorphisms φ_ij:U_ij→U_ji, with U_ii=X_i, such that the overlaps are compatible on triples and φ_ik=φ_jk∘φ_ij wherever both compositions are defined.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: closed subscheme of an affine scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A closed subscheme of the affine scheme Spec(R) is a scheme isomorphic over Spec(R) to Spec(R/I) for some ideal I⊆R, equipped with the closed immersion induced by the quotient map R→R/I.

observations.context_hint: Topology: specialization relation between points
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For points x and y in a topological space X, x is a specialization of y when x lies in the closure of the singleton {y}; equivalently y is a generalization of x.

observations.context_hint: Topology: subset stable under specialization
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A subset T⊆X is stable under specialization if whenever y∈T and x lies in the closure of {y}, then x also belongs to T.

observations.context_hint: Topology: subset stable under generalization
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A subset T⊆X is stable under generalization if it contains every generalization y of each point x that it contains.

observations.context_hint: Topology: specializing continuous map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is specializing if every specialization f(x′)⇝y in Y can be lifted to a specialization x′⇝x in X with f(x)=y.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is generalizing if any generalization y′⇝f(x) in Y lifts to a generalization x′⇝x in X with f(x′)=y′.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: cartesian arrow over a base category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a functor p:E→C, a morphism φ:y→x in E is strongly p-cartesian if for every object z in E, each pair consisting of a map ψ:z→x and a base arrow p(z)→p(y) that composes with p(φ) to p(ψ) factors uniquely through φ.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: Grothendieck fibration

observations.context_hint: Module theory: universally injective or pure monomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A homomorphism f:M→N of R-modules is universally injective if for every R-module Q the induced tensor map f⊗id_Q:M⊗_R Q→N⊗_R Q is injective.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: pure short exact sequence
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A short exact sequence 0→M_1→M_2→M_3→0 of R-modules is universally exact if the first nonzero arrow M_1→M_2 remains injective after tensoring with any R-module; equivalently the entire sequence remains exact after every such tensor product.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: reduced scheme
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A scheme X is reduced if each local ring O_{X,x} is a reduced ring, meaning it contains no nonzero nilpotent element.

observations.text: Equivalently, a scheme X is reduced exactly when the ring O_X(U) has no nonzero nilpotent elements for every open subset U of X.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: reduced induced structure on a closed subset
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a closed subset T of a scheme X, its reduced induced closed subscheme is the unique reduced closed subscheme of X whose underlying topological space equals T.
