observations.source_section: Section 3.10 introduction of sets with a group action
observations.text: A left action of a group G on a set X is a map G×X→X such that e·x=x for all x and (gh)·x=g·(h·x) for every g,h∈G and x∈X.

observations.context_hint: Group theory: equivariant map between sets with a G-action
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: If X and Y are G-sets, a G-equivariant map f:X→Y is a function satisfying f(g·x)=g·f(x) for every g∈G and x∈X.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: geometrically reduced algebra
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.source_section: Section 10.43 definition of geometrically reduced k-algebra
observations.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically reduced if for every field extension K/k the tensor-product K-algebra A⊗_k K is a reduced ring.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: perfect-closure criterion for geometric reducedness
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Equivalently, A is geometrically reduced over k if A⊗_k k^perf is reduced, where k^perf denotes the perfect closure of k; this is a field-extension test of the same property.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: characterization of projectivity using flatness and Mittag-Leffler modules
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is projective if and only if it is flat and Mittag-Leffler and is isomorphic to a direct sum of countably generated R-modules.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: finite ring map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: étale ring map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: local étaleness at a target prime

observations.text: A ring map R→S is étale at a prime q∈Spec(S) if there is an element g∈S\q such that the localized ring map R→S_g is étale.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: equalizer of two parallel arrows

observations.text: Given parallel morphisms f,g:X⇉Y in a category C, an equalizer is a morphism e:E→X such that f∘e=g∘e and any h:Z→X satisfying f∘h=g∘h factors uniquely through e.

observations.context_hint: Order theory: preorder and preordered set

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

observations.text: An irreducible component of a topological space X is a maximal irreducible subset of X under inclusion; every such component is closed.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A generic point of an irreducible closed subset Z of a topological space X is a point η∈Z such that the closure of {η} equals Z.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For distinct points x,y of a topological space, y is an immediate specialization of x if y lies in the closure of {x} and no third point lies between x and y in the specialization relation.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A dimension function on a topological space X is an integer-valued map δ:X→Z that strictly decreases on nontrivial specializations and drops by exactly one for immediate specializations.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: formal smoothness of a field extension
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A field extension K/k is formally smooth over k when every k-algebra map K→A/I across a square-zero quotient lifts to A. In positive characteristic this is equivalent to separability of K/k; in characteristic zero every field extension satisfies it.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: localization of a category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A localization of a category C at a multiplicative system S is a category S^{-1}C with functor Q:C→S^{-1}C making each s∈S invertible and universal among functors from C that invert all s∈S.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: multiplicative system of arrows
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A multiplicative system of arrows in a category contains all identities, is closed under composition, and satisfies both left and right Ore-square completion and the corresponding cancellation axioms.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: coprime polynomials
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Polynomials f,g∈k[x] over a field k are relatively prime when the ideal (f,g) they generate is the entire polynomial ring k[x].

observations.context_hint: Field theory: common-root coprimality test
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Two polynomials f,g over a field k are relatively prime if and only if they have no common zero in an algebraic closure of k.

observations.context_hint: Topology: Hausdorff space
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological space X is Hausdorff if every pair of distinct points has disjoint open neighbourhoods.

observations.context_hint: Topology: closed diagonal characterization
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A topological space X is Hausdorff exactly when the diagonal {(x,x):x∈X} is a closed subset of X×X with its product topology.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: flat module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is flat when the tensor functor −⊗_R M carries every exact sequence of R-modules to an exact sequence.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: faithfully flat module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An R-module M is faithfully flat if tensoring with M preserves and reflects exactness of arbitrary sequences of R-modules.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: flat ring map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is flat if S is flat as an R-module via the given homomorphism.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: faithfully flat ring map
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is faithfully flat if S is faithfully flat as an R-module under the ring map.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Cohen–Macaulay local module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A finitely generated module M over a Noetherian local ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R(M) equals the Krull dimension of the support Supp_R(M).

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: maximal Cohen–Macaulay module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R(M)=dim(R), not merely the dimension of its possibly smaller support.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: global Cohen–Macaulay module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A finite module M over a Noetherian ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if for each prime p the localized module M_p is Cohen–Macaulay over the local ring R_p.

observations.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: affine scheme morphisms and ring maps
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For commutative rings A and B, a morphism Spec(B)→Spec(A) of affine schemes is equivalently determined by a ring homomorphism A→B, acting on prime ideals by inverse image.

observations.context_hint: Higher category theory: strict 2-category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A strict 2-category consists of objects, hom-categories whose objects are 1-morphisms and arrows are 2-morphisms, and strictly associative and unital composition functors between hom-categories satisfying the interchange law.

observations.context_hint: Higher category theory: equivalence of 2-category objects
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: Two objects X,Y in a 2-category are equivalent if there are 1-morphisms F:X→Y and G:Y→X with invertible 2-morphisms FG⇒id_Y and GF⇒id_X.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: irreducible components of the prime spectrum
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a commutative ring R, the irreducible components of Spec(R) are exactly the subsets V(p) where p ranges over prime ideals minimal under inclusion.

observations.context_hint: Topology: constructible subset using retrocompact opens
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A subset E of a topological space X is constructible if it is a finite union of sets U\V with U and V open and retrocompact in X.

observations.context_hint: Topology: locally constructible subset
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A subset E of X is locally constructible if there exists an open cover (V_i) of X such that E∩V_i is constructible as a subset of V_i for each i.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: monomorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is a monomorphism if for every object W and maps a,b:W→X, the equality f∘a=f∘b implies a=b.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: epimorphism
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is an epimorphism if for every object W and maps a,b:Y→W, equality a∘f=b∘f implies a=b.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: groupoid-valued presheaf
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A groupoid-valued presheaf on a category C is a contravariant pseudofunctor assigning a groupoid F(U) to each object U of C and compatible pullback functors F(U)→F(V) to arrows V→U.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: split category fibred in groupoids
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A category fibred in groupoids over C is split if it is isomorphic over C to the Grothendieck construction associated with a strict contravariant functor C→Groupoids.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: regular sequence on a module
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A finite sequence f_1,…,f_r in a ring R is M-regular for an R-module M if f_i acts injectively on M/(f_1,…,f_{i-1})M for every i and the final quotient M/(f_1,…,f_r)M is nonzero.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: symbolic powers of prime ideals
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R and n≥0, the nth symbolic power p^(n) is the contraction to R of p^n R_p, equivalently the kernel of R→R_p/p^nR_p.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: complete local ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A local ring (R,m) is complete if the canonical homomorphism R→lim_n R/m^n is an isomorphism; equivalently, its m-adic completion introduces no new elements.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: coefficient ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For a complete local ring (R,m) with residue characteristic p, a coefficient ring is a complete local subring Λ⊆R inducing an isomorphism of residue fields and satisfying Λ∩m=pΛ.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Cohen ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A Cohen ring is a complete discrete valuation ring whose maximal ideal is generated by a prime integer p.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: going-up property
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring map R→S satisfies going up if, given p⊆p′ in Spec(R) and q∈Spec(S) above p, some prime q′⊇q of S lies above p′.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: going-down property
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A ring map R→S satisfies going down if, given p⊆p′ in Spec(R) and q′ of S lying above p′, a prime q⊆q′ exists that lies over p.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: category-valued presheaf
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A category-valued presheaf on C is a contravariant functor C^op→Cat, assigning a category to each object and compatible pullback functors to arrows in the base.

observations.context_hint: Category theory: split fibred category
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A fibred category p:E→C is split if it is isomorphic over C to the Grothendieck construction of a strictly contravariant category-valued functor on C.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: valuation ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: An integral domain V with fraction field K is a valuation ring if each nonzero x∈K has at least one of x and x^{-1} lying in V.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: domination of local rings
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: For local subrings A⊆B of a common field, B dominates A if the maximal ideal of B contracts to the maximal ideal of A.

observations.context_hint: Commutative algebra: discrete valuation ring
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring in the Stacks convention if its associated ordered value group is isomorphic to Z, with its usual order.

observations.context_hint: Field theory: perfect field
observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: A field k is perfect if every algebraic field extension of k is separable over k; equivalently k has characteristic zero or, in characteristic p>0, every element of k is a pth power.

observations.reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
observations.text: The perfect closure of a field k of positive characteristic p is its smallest perfect extension obtained by adjoining all compatible p-power roots of elements of k inside a fixed algebraic closure.

observations.text: An ordinal is a transitive set α on which the membership relation ∈ is a well-order: each nonempty subset has an ∈-least element, and every member of α is itself a subset of α.

observations.text: The successor of an ordinal α is the ordinal α+1=α∪{α}; an ordinal is a successor ordinal if it has this form for some α.

observations.text: An ordinal λ is a limit ordinal if it is nonzero and is not the successor of any other ordinal.

observations.text: A nonnegatively graded ring S is a direct sum S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n of additive groups satisfying S_nS_m⊆S_{n+m} for every n,m≥0.

observations.text: The degree shift M(n) of a graded module M is the graded module whose degree-j component is M(n)_j=M_{n+j}, preserving the ungraded module structure.

observations.context_hint: Module theory: projective module

observations.text: An R-module P is projective if the covariant functor Hom_R(P,−) is exact; equivalently every R-linear map P→N lifts across every surjective module map M→N.

observations.text: An R-module M is locally free if Spec(R) admits a cover by standard opens D(f_i) such that each localization M_{f_i} is free over R_{f_i}.

observations.text: An R-module M is finite projective exactly when it is finitely generated and projective; equivalently M is a direct summand of R^n for some finite n, or finite locally free.

observations.text: For a category C, the opposite category C^op has the same objects as C and a morphism X→Y in C^op for each morphism Y→X in C, with composition reversed.
